381YE Summer Solstice Imperial elections.d: New or returning senators were chosen for nine territories. Most Military Council generals were re-elected, though new generals took the Tusks, Black Thorns, Army of the Northern Eagle and Bounders. The Wolves of War was left under the Throne after Gabriel Barossa was removed using the Throne's power as Defender of the Empire. The Synod appointed cardinals of Courage, Wisdom and Loyalty, and Martin Orchard became Imperial Inquisitor. Conclave grandmasters and the Archmage of Spring were named. The Damatian Cliffs went at auction for the highest bid of 355 thrones. The Sheriff of Overton was no longer in Imperial hands, and the Overseer of the Cavabianca Dock was held over to Autumn.

n.Dawn: Lady Eve of House Orzel became Senator for Weirwater and Zoran Orzel was returned as General of the Golden Sun. Abaddon De Rondell of Dawn was named Cardinal of Wisdom.
n.Highguard: Sammual took the Bastion Senate seat and Mathayus kept the Granite Pillar. Highborn also won the Cardinal of Loyalty (Caleb of Reumah's Redoubt) and the Virtue Inquisitor of Courage (Lucifer, Son of Cyrus), while Sariel provisionally retained the Wisdom inquisitorship.
n.Navarr: Llewellyn Leafstalker was returned as Senator for Miaren and Eira Pridestalker became General of the Black Thorns. Corwin Leafstalker provisionally retained the Virtue Inquisitor of Loyalty.
n.The Brass Coast: Chiara i Zaydan i Riqueza became Senator for Feroz and Estana i Mestiere i Guerra was returned as General of the Red Wind Corsairs. Safya i Kalamar i Guerra took the Glass Parador.
n.The League: Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos held the Sarvos seat, Will Talbot kept the Drakes and a Sarvos citizen became Imperial Consul. The Wolves of War passed to the Throne after its general, Gabriel Barossa, was removed, and the Cavabianca Dock overseer was held over to Autumn.
n.The Marches: William Guildenstern became Senator for Mitwold and new generals took the Tusks and the Bounders. Martin Orchard of the Marches became Imperial Inquisitor, but the Sheriff of Overton was recorded as no longer in Imperial hands.
n.Urizen: Probus of Shattered Spire was returned as Senator for Redoubt and Nicassia Abicia kept the Citadel Guard. Alcuin of the Spire of Shattered Art was named Head Gardener of Urizen.
n.Varushka: Pipski of the Vor'ezi became Senator for Karov and Amris of Varushka was named Gatekeeper of Wisdom. Vtaly Grigorovich Dukov kept the Granites of Veltsgorsk.
n.Wintermark: Atte was returned as Senator for Sermersuaq and Irontide Skar kept the Summer Storm. Kai of Wintermark was named Guardian of Dunfrith.

t.Bastion: Sammual was elected Senator for Bastion.
t.Feroz: Chiara i Zaydan i Riqueza was elected Senator for Feroz.
t.Karov: Pipski of the Vor'ezi was elected Senator for Karov.
t.Miaren: Incumbent Llewellyn Leafstalker was returned as Senator for Miaren.
t.Mitwold: William Guildenstern was elected Senator for Mitwold.
t.Redoubt: Incumbent Probus of Shattered Spire was returned as Senator for Redoubt.
t.Sarvos: Incumbent Magdelena Alanga Di Sarvos kept the Senate seat for Sarvos.
t.Sermersuaq: Incumbent Atte was returned as Senator for Sermersuaq.
t.Weirwater: Lady Eve of House Orzel was elected Senator for Weirwater.

381YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: Dawn's National Assembly declared Empress Lisabetta Queen of Dawn, and the Throne addressed all citizens. Seven nations denounced Yael of Highguard as false, while Highguard and Dawn embraced her and the Imperial Orcs stood aside. A sinkhole swallowed parts of Temeschwar, Miaren, Upwold and Hahnmark, though a Navarr vates warning prevented major loss of life. Imperial magicians could no longer draw power from Spring regio. A fishing boom offered risky opportunities in the Bay of Catazar. The Grendel discovered the Freeborn lost colony on Zemress. The Mournwold situation worsened. Other entries covered the Iron Helms mandates, Winds of Magic, curiosities for sale in Anvil, eternal responses and trade.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish National Assembly recognised Empress Lisabetta as Queen of Dawn, with profound potential repercussions. Dawn also embraced Yael despite apparent internal doubt.
n.Grendel: Grendel threatened fisherfolk seeking the fishing boom in the Bay of Catazar, and they had discovered the Freeborn colony on the Isle of Zemress, whose people faced the salt mines of Dubhtraig.
n.Highguard: Highguard embraced Yael's claims to be the reborn First Empress as the schism neared its climax. Highguard was also among the nations tagged for the Catazar fishing opportunity.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs made clear they had no part in the conflict over Yael and Human destiny.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun castles and armies were noted as part of the complicated and worsening situation in the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: Navarr sent priests to denounce Yael and was caught up in the Iron Helms controversy. A band of Navarr vates gave the timely warning that averted major loss of life in the sinkhole.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn denounced Yael and were tagged for the Catazar fishing opportunity. They also faced the plight of their lost cousins on Zemress, now discovered by the Grendel.
n.The League: The League denounced Yael and was tagged for the Catazar fishing boom. League-held Temeschwar was struck by the great sinkhole.
n.The Marches: The Marches denounced Yael and were involved in the Iron Helms controversy. Marcher-held Upwold was partly swallowed by the sinkhole.
n.Urizen: Urizen denounced Yael and was tagged for the fishing opportunity. A burning plume of fire and shadows appeared in Urizen-held Redoubt.
n.Varushka: Varushka's new army, the Iron Helms, became the focus of controversial mandates following statements of principle about its role. Varushka also denounced Yael.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark denounced Yael and was drawn into the Iron Helms mandates. Wintermark-held Hahnmark was partly swallowed by the sinkhole.

t.Bay of Catazar: A boom in fish and sea creatures, credited to Spring magic and storms, offered Bay fisherfolk a lucrative but risky opportunity, given the Grendel threat.
t.Hahnmark: Part of Hahnmark was swallowed by the massive sinkhole that struck the north-western Empire.
t.Miaren: Part of Miaren was swallowed by the sinkhole, with the chasm stretching as far as the orchards of Goldglades.
t.Mournwold: The situation in the Mournwold grew increasingly complicated, with a storm brewing alongside Jotun castles and armies. Peculiar cauldron shenanigans there were also reported.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Winds of Magic noted a burning plume of fire and shadows in Redoubt.
t.Temeschwar: Part of Temeschwar was swallowed by the sinkhole, with the chasm running from near Eastern Guard deep into the Vardstein Vale.
t.Upwold: Part of Upwold was swallowed by the great sinkhole, though a Navarr warning prevented major loss of life.

r.Miaren/Goldglades: The great chasm left by the sinkhole stretched to the orchards of Goldglades.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: The chasm ran from a point dangerously close to Eastern Guard deep into the wild hunting grounds of the Vardstein Vale.

381YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: The Freeborn Storm retook the Grendel-held spires of Naris, but most of Evenstar's healers had already been enslaved. The Golden Sun won every clash with a growing unliving horde in Weirwater but could not destroy it, as fallen Dawnish rose to join it. In Spiral, the Towerjacks, Green Shield and Eastern Sky held Cinion while the Fire of the South pushed into Ossuary. The Black Thorns raided Hordalant, were driven back into Liathaven and are now surrounded. Marcher-led armies liberated two Mournwold regions and neared a third, but were shunned by local people. The Druj razed the Towers of Dawn, took Dawnguard, and seized Lustri and Occursion, burning Endsmeet.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun fought a draining campaign against the unliving in Weirwater, while the Eastern Sky helped hold Cinion and the Hounds of Glory and Gryphon's Pride fought in the Mournwold. Dawnguard fell to the Druj, the Towers of Dawn were destroyed and noble houses including de Carsenere, Martel, Aurelius and Vexille were overrun.
n.Druj: Despite the peace treaty agreed six months earlier, Druj armies razed the Towers of Dawn and took Drycastle and Dawnguard. In Zenith they seized Lustri and Occursion, burned Endsmeet and raised a powerful Penumbral Veil over the territory.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost their foothold in Naris and were held at Cinion. Their eastern turtle-banner force was driven back into Ossuary by the Fire of the South, although they still hold ground in Spiral.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched through Casinea and Bastion, and veterans of the liberation of Reikos are referred to.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun joined the Mournwold offensive as the only army present from a nation that had not declared against the Land without Tears.
n.Jotun: The Jotun drove the Black Thorns out of Hordalant and surrounded them in Liathaven with a vastly larger force. In the Mournwold their much-reduced forces gave up Freemoor and the Chalkdowns, losing around three times as many troops as the Empire.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns' raid into Hordalant disrupted Jotun resupply but ended with the army trapped and facing heavy losses in Liathaven. The Quiet Step fought brutally with poison, traps and assassinations in the Mournwold.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Storm liberated Naris and stormed Evenstar. The Fire of the South made a forced march across the Empire to surprise the Grendel in Ossuary.
n.The League: The Towerjacks, fighting under a potent enchantment, blunted the main Grendel thrust on Cinion from Ateri, though their refusal to give any ground cost many lives.
n.The Marches: All four Marcher armies fought together in the Mournwold for the first time and liberated much of the north-east. Local Marchers met them with sullen shunning and accusations of murder and cowardice.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are listed among the barbarian nations the Empire has not seriously attacked at home since Empress Brannan's reign.
n.Urizen: Naris was freed, but Evenstar's healers were carried off as slaves. Imperial armies held Cinion, while in Zenith the Druj took Lustri and Occursion, gutted Endsmeet and attacked Proceris.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle half-repaired Redoubt's roads, while the Golden Axe and Iron Helms fought in the Mournwold, where the Iron Helms gained a reputation for mutilating fallen Jotun. Varushkan corpses also formed much of the unliving horde in Weirwater.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark warriors defending southern Cinion heard the stirring Black Plateau in their dreams. Conjunctions west of Sermersuaq offer a chance to skirmish with the Jotun.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun marched from Astolat into Weirwater, and the unliving's earlier foray there is recalled.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South passed through Bastion on its forced march east.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Grendel pirate ships carried slaves from Evenstar across the Bay of Catazar.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: breaking north into Bregasland is one costly escape route open to the trapped Black Thorns.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South pressed through Casinea en route to Spiral.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant's roads and farms are compared to those of Hahnmark.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks recalled their defence of Holberg, and some Dawnguard refugees fled into Holmauer.
t.Hordalant: The Black Thorns made brief gains in Vallorberg and disrupted Jotun resupply before fortifications and armies drove them out, leaving Hordalant in Jotun hands.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr's previous slip from Kahraman into Liathaven is recalled.
t.Liathaven: The retreating Black Thorns are surrounded by a Jotun force up to five times their size and face thousands of casualties. Two conjunctions may offer ways to help them.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched through Miaren.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is likened to Mitwold.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South passed through Morrow into Zenith.
t.Mournwold: A large Imperial host liberated Freemoor and the Chalkdowns and nearly took Alderly. Mournwold civilians are deeply angry with the Empire.
t.Redoubt: The Freeborn Storm liberated the Grendel-held spires of Naris. The Northern Eagle is halfway through restoring the storm-damaged roads, while the Granite Pillar guards the north.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: veterans of Reikos's liberation fear for those left in Dawnguard.
t.Semmerholm: Hawthorne sent pleas for aid into Semmerholm, and Dawnguard refugees fled north into the forests of Axmure.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: small conjunctions lead to locations west of Sermersuaq, culminating in a Jotun skirmish.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Helms came to the Mournwold fresh from a militia engagement in Skarsind.
t.Spiral: The Empire held Cinion against a three-pronged Grendel assault, and the Fire of the South began driving the orcs out of Ossuary. The Black Plateau in Screed is stirring.
t.Tassato: Imperial armies regrouped in Tassato after losing the Greensward, then marched north through Madeiras.
t.The Barrens: The Druj destroyed the Towers of Dawn, took Drycastle and conquered Dawnguard, leaving the Barrens a conquered territory.
t.The Semmerlak: Drowned fisherfolk and stranger things rose from the mud of the Semmerlak to attack Culwich.
t.Upwold: The Imperial host gathered in an armed camp on the Heath before invading the Mournwold.
t.Weirwater: The dead rose across Weirwater, killing hundreds and adding a thousand Dawnish husks to the horde. The Golden Sun saved Hawthorne but could not destroy the unliving.
t.Zenith: The Druj conquered Lustri and Occursion, gutted Endsmeet and are attacking Proceris under a Penumbral Veil, and the Starlight Drift, Tower of the Fall and Origen's Rest are lost.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Druj demolition of the Great Pits of Ennerlund is recalled.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: A few nobles led a band of Dawnguard refugees through the mountains into Holmauer.
r.Hordalant/Vallorberg: The Black Thorns seized farmsteads here before Jotun forces drove them back across the Volg and out of the territory.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: A massive Jotun force was waiting here for the retreating Black Thorns, and two conjunctions are expected to open here.
r.Liathaven/Western Scout: Escape south into Western Scout via the Paths of Lan Thúven is a costly option for the Black Thorns, as the Jotun now hold Silent Stand steading.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: The Empire is about three-quarters of the way to taking Alderly despite Feni ambushers. Villagers in Charcoal drove soldiers off with banging pans.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Chalkdowns were liberated from the Jotun.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Freemoor was liberated, but locals, including Blackheath's tanners, shunned the Imperial armies.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Jotun forces fell back west to Green March, where a conjunction of uncertain advantage will open.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: During the Spring Equinox the Jotun completed driving Imperial armies out of the Greensward into Tassato.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: Retreating Jotun fell back to their castles in the Ore Hills.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Retreating Jotun fell back to their castles in Southmoor.
r.Redoubt/Naris: The Freeborn Storm retook the southern spires and stormed Evenstar, though most of its healers had already been enslaved.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: Mentioned in passing: the Eastern Sky marched through the passes of Willstone to Cinion.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: Refugees fleeing the Druj conquest of Dawnguard escaped north into the forests of Axmure.
r.Spiral/Ateri: The main Grendel thrust from Ateri towards Damakan's Forge was countered by the Towerjacks.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Three Imperial armies held Cinion against the Grendel, though some Grendel presence remains on its eastern side.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: The Fire of the South surprised the Grendel and began pushing south through Ossuary. A conjunction offers a chance to fight Grendel soldiers here.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Grendel were repeatedly pushed back into Screed, and its Black Plateau is stirring amid the bloodshed.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies marched north through the forests of Madeiras.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: one Druj force swept into Dawnguard from Murderdale.
r.Upwold/The Heath: The Imperial host made its armed camp on the Heath near Sutton Stone Quarries before invading the Mournwold.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Mentioned in passing: armies marched through Tower March on their way to Upwold.
r.Weirwater/Hawksmoor: The unliving horde gathered here, besieged Hawthorne, and was driven off by the Golden Sun at a terrible cost.
r.Weirwater/Weirmoor: Ancient dead rose from a battlefield in northern Weirmoor, and the Golden Sun entered Weirwater through its forests.
r.Zenith/Lustri: An overwhelming Druj force from the Mallum overran Lustri, silencing spires such as Gatherwood.
r.Zenith/Occursion: The Druj conquered Occursion, burning resisting spires and taking key sites, and Endsmeet was gutted.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Endsmeet's survivors fled into Proceris with the Druj close behind. A conjunction here may help refugees threatened by a Grendel advance force.

Abrogate motion to construct the Signori.d: Earlier in the Summer 381YE summit the Senate had passed a motion to construct a vineyard in Sarvos, the Signori d'Argento Vineyards, as a sinecure providing money. Later in the same summit Kahraman proposed abrogating that motion, Zenith seconded it, and the abrogation passed, cancelling the commission. The vineyard did not stay cancelled: it was later recommissioned by Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower, acting as holder of an Imperial Wayleave.

n.The League: The League lost, then regained, a planned Imperial vineyard sinecure in its territory of Sarvos when the Senate's commission was abrogated and the project was later recommissioned through an Imperial Wayleave.

t.Sarvos: The Signori d'Argento Vineyards planned for Sarvos were cancelled by this abrogation, though the vineyard was later recommissioned by Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower.

Accept Orcs of the Great Forest treaty.d: Proposed by Holberg and seconded by Feroz, the motion passed and survived Constitutional Court scrutiny. The treaty, negotiated at the Spring Equinox summit by Miroslav di Sarvos and the Speaker of Totems, lets the Great Forest live as guests of the Navarr in the Lower Tarn Valley for five years, hunting, building and trading. In return they will defend Therunin and fight alongside Navarri armies in the Barrens under their own warchief, sharing knowledge of the Druj through a Military Liaison. They may practise their religion privately but not proselytise. Should the Barrens fall to the Empire, the valley returns to Imperial control and the Heart of Peytaht is ceded to the Great Forest.

n.Druj: The treaty binds the Great Forest to make common cause against Druj attack and to share their knowledge of the Druj with the Empire, though they may take no action against the Druj while the Empire is at peace with them, save in self-defence.
n.Navarr: The Navarr host the Great Forest orcs as guests in Therunin for five years, gaining allies who will fight alongside any Navarri army in the Barrens; Navarri may walk the trods freely through the leased land but may not hunt there.

t.Therunin: Therunin gains orc defenders sworn to protect the territory for the duration of the treaty, while its Imperial residents keep their right to live and gather resources there.

r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Lower Tarn Valley becomes the leased home of the Great Forest orcs for five years, where they may hunt, build and trade, and where Imperial citizens may stay under the Way or leave with guaranteed safe passage.

All along the watchtower.d: Imperial troops in the Mourn were shunned or driven off with rough music. Locals accused the Empire of caring only about killing Jotun. A landskeeper plan to have Rivers of Life cast failed when the Empire lost access to Spring regio. The Marcher assembly's statement on punishments was undercut when the Conclave added another Spring curse to lore. The civil service identified several options. One was a proposed Declaration of Remorse, costing 25 thrones per ritual, to destroy every text of Rivers Run Red and Mountain Remembers its Youth. Others were making the Singing Caves a Marcher national seat, a no-retreat mandate, and 75 thrones a season to feed orc thralls. A harsher alternative was a Senate law letting armies Lay Down the Law. In the end the Marcher assembly passed the mandate, and Mel of Mourn spread it with liao.

n.Jotun: Jotun forces in the Mourn were falling back in terror before the Iron Helms' onslaught. The orc thralls they had brought with them were left trapped, short of food and in growing danger from Imperial armies.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named as a neighbouring territory, and the Hierro clan is cited as an example of the risks of encouraging virtue.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Mournwolders assumed a League prince would end up holding the Singing Caves. Holberg is cited as land that joined the League only after Dawnish conquest.
n.The Marches: Marchers in the Mourn grew deeply alienated from the Empire over the curses and the war. The Marcher assembly then passed a mandate that no Marcher army can ever again give ground, a gesture of solidarity with the Mournwolders.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher assembly's statement notes that the Urizen General was rebuked by the Synod over the cursing of the Mourn.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms under General Akstis Eigulys used visible, merciless tactics against Jotun warriors and spared civilians, yet left Mournwolders fearful of what fresh orders might bring. Empress Varkula's letter to a Karsk senator is also quoted.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: named alongside Upwold and Mitwold as Marcher lands whose shared resolve to defend their land the no-retreat mandate would show.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of a land that joined the Empire only after Dawnish armies conquered the surrounding territory.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory across the border with whose people some Mourn thralls have less in common than with their orc neighbours.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: a letter from Empress Varkula to a Karsk senator is quoted.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Harry Archer, a thresher from Mitwold, devised the proposed Declaration of Remorse, and Mitwold is named among the Marcher lands the mandate would align with the Mourn.
t.Mournwold: With Imperial armies driving out the Jotun, the Mournwold seethed with anger over the curse deaths and the Iron Helms' brutality. Imperial soldiers were shunned and orc thralls were left hungry, leaving the territory close to rebellion once the armies depart.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: named as a territory across the border with whose people some Mourn thralls have less in common than with their orc neighbours.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: named alongside Mitwold and Bregasland as Marcher lands whose shared resolve to defend their land the no-retreat mandate would show.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: Overton in Greensward had held out against the Jotun. The Singing Caves mithril mine near Overton was proposed as a Marcher national seat, after the Senate's earlier allocation to the Marchers had been vetoed by the Throne.
r.Tassato/Madeiras: Mentioned in passing: a tinker reports that the failure of Spring regio was being felt in Madeiras as well.

Amend the use of the Imperial breadbaske.d: The motion changed the entire function of the Imperial Breadbasket great work to providing food for the people of the Mournwold. While it stands, the work provides no funds to farmers in the Marches, and its granaries no longer reduce the effects of natural decay on the armies of a single nation. The change took three months to take effect. If the motion is abrogated, the money for Marcher farms would be restored immediately, but restoring the protection against natural decay for a nation's armies would take a further three months, during which all armies would suffer the full effect of decay.

n.Jotun: The Jotun-held Mournwold became the beneficiary of the Imperial Breadbasket, which would now supply food to the people living under Jotun rule there.

t.Mournwold: The Imperial Breadbasket was redirected to provide free food to the people of the Mournwold who were not in an army, at a time when the territory was held by the Jotun.

Archive:381YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg also commanded the League's Wolves of War after using the Defender of the Empire power. Every Imperial nation's senators and generals are listed, along with the Senate's ambassadors, sinecures and ministries. The Synod's cardinals, gatekeepers and virtue inquisitors are recorded, as are the six Archmagi, the Conclave's Grandmasters and the Bourse seats with their winning bids. Several posts stood vacant, including the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, the Dean of Pilgrims, the Eternal Flame of Miaren and the Custodian of the Imperial War Memorial. The Civilian Commissioners had been abrogated at the Winter Solstice 380YE. Foreign powers held two national Bourse seats: the Thule held the Stonefield Ice Caves and the Grendel held the Legacy.

n.Dawn: Dawn held three Senate seats, four generals, the Cardinal of Wisdom (Agnetha De Rondell) and the post of High Bard of the Empire (Kaywenn du Launcet).
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are recorded as holding the Legacy, a Urizen national Bourse position.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four Senate seats, three generals, the Cardinals of Loyalty and Pride, and several Synod and Conclave posts, including Imperial Magus and Bursar of the Conclave.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held the Skarsind Senate seat (Irontide Vio), two generals, the Cardinal of the Way (Atla) and the post of Chaplain Consular.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three Senate seats, two generals, and the Military Council posts of Warmage and Quartermaster General of the Imperial Armies.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held four Senate seats, two generals and an admiral, and its Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra served as Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: The League held the Throne through Empress Lisabetta Giacomi von Holberg, who also led the Wolves of War. It held four Senate seats and the Cardinals of Ambition and Vigilance.
n.The Marches: The Marches held three Senate seats and four generals, and Martin Orchard of the Marches served as Imperial Inquisitor.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule are recorded as holding the Stonefield Ice Caves, a Wintermark national Bourse position.
n.Urizen: Urizen held three Senate seats and a single general, Nicassia Avicia of the Citadel Guard. Its people included the High Exorcist and the Archmage of Night.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four Senate seats and three generals, and Simargl of Varushka served as Dean of the Lyceum.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held three Senate seats, two generals, the Cardinal of Courage (Jorma Steelhail) and the Conscience of the Senate (Ingrid Sigeing).

t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Atte.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Irontide Vio. Irontide T'onk served as Preceptor of the Skarsind College of Warcasting.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato. Edwin Sanguineo di Tassato held the ministry of Steward of the Tassato Mana Exchange.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Gant Archama.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Willa Farkus-Vigil.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Henry Ward.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Vuk the Wolfeater.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Lady Eve Orzel. The Weirwater Vales were held by Jack Plank.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: listed with its senator, Edmundo of Endsmeet.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Great Pits of Ennerlund Bourse seat is recorded as held by Lukash Biessek von Temeschwar for 590 Thrones.

Changing of the guards.d: Tamain Sepulchre's Statement of Principle, upheld 158–20, inspired the advocate Melusine of Tanner's Bar to propose that Dawn's senatorial tourneys be judged by the Queen or her representative, who would pick the winning house. Lady Griffinsbain, speaking as egregore, said support was real but not universal. Melusine therefore sought a mandate with 100 doses of liao, which would give the Empress's seasonal words the weight of a greater-majority Statement in Dawn. Weirwater's Five Rings cabal would then surrender the Staff of the Archmage schema, and Castle Spiral would kneel to her. Separately, Earl du Chailly sought a potentially heretical mandate urging glory above virtue. Both were opportunities available only during the Summer Solstice 381YE.

n.Dawn: Dawn faced a choice between partially restoring the monarchy, with the Queen judging senatorial tourneys and her words carrying national authority, and a riskier call to put glory before virtue. The latter would bolster Dawnish military units but weaken congregations and risk Synod condemnation.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel are not named on the page; their only connection is that they held Spiral, whose castle residents offered fealty to a ruling Queen of Dawn.

t.Spiral: The residents of Castle Spiral pledged to acknowledge Lisabetta as their liege if she became the ultimate authority in Dawn. At her command they would pass the castle's resources to the Castellan of Spiral Castle, either to keep resupplying Imperial armies or to dispose of its weirwood directly.
t.Weirwater: The secretive Five Rings weaver's cabal of Weirwater offered to hand the Queen the six schema for the Staff of the Archmage, held in trust since King Rodric, if she became Queen in truth. This could cost the Archmages a symbol of their office.

Construct Embassy to the Thule.d: Proposed by the Volodmartz senator and seconded by the Karsk senator, the motion called for an embassy to the Thule of Otkodov to be built in Miekarova at no cost to the Imperial treasury. After the Summer Solstice, Vuk The Wolfeater provided the materials and funds: 25 wains of weirwood, 25 wains of white granite and 12 thrones. The embassy was due to be complete from the start of the Autumn Equinox. The Senate had already appointed the first Ambassador to Otkodov, who would use the new building.

n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov were to gain a dedicated Imperial embassy just across their border in Miekarova, housing the Empire's Ambassador to them.
n.Varushka: The embassy was to be built on Varushkan soil in Miekarova, with the motion proposed and seconded by the senators for Volodmartz and Karsk and the materials supplied by Vuk The Wolfeater.

t.Miekarova: Miekarova was chosen as the site of the new Imperial embassy to the Thule, due for completion by the Autumn Equinox.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov was the destination of the embassy, which was built to serve the Empire's newly appointed Ambassador to Otkodov.

Construct a Trade Hub to Axos.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Sarvos, the motion granted permission to build a Trade Hub to Axos in Necropolis. It was passed. The resulting ministry exchanges liao for mana and other materials from Axos, and its holder is assigned by the Loyalty assembly. After the Summer Solstice 381YE, Tarquinius provided 20 wains of white granite and 5 thrones towards its construction. Completing the ministry automatically created the title of Quaymaster of the Black Sails.

n.Highguard: Highguard gains an Imperial trade link to Axos sited in its own territory of Necropolis, through which liao can be exchanged for mana.

t.Necropolis: Necropolis was chosen as the site of the Trade Hub to Axos, which brings an Imperial ministry trading liao for mana into the territory, along with the new title of Quaymaster of the Black Sails.

Construct a reliquary in the mountains o.d: Azzam i Zaydan i Requeza, a holder of an Imperial Wayleave, used the power to commission constructions that the Senate had delegated to them to announce a reliquary in the mountains of Gildermark. It takes the form of a mana sinecure called the Weigher of Worth. The Senator of Skarsind appoints the holder, and the Imperial Orc National Assembly can revoke the title. After the Summer Solstice 381YE, Azzam i Zaydan i Riqueza provided the 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns needed. The sinecure was completed and automatically created the title Weigher of Worth.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc National Assembly holds the power to revoke the new Weigher of Worth title. The Senator of Skarsind appoints its holder.

t.Skarsind: Skarsind gained a new mana sinecure, the Weigher of Worth. Its holder is appointed by the territory's Senator.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: The completed reliquary stands in the mountains of Gildermark, built using 10 wains of mithril.

Construct a road connecting the Thule to.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by the senator for Temeschwar, the motion called for a road connecting the Thule to the Torfast Trading Post. It cost 30 wains of white granite and 60 crowns in labour, and took six months to construct. Both were provided by Irontide Vio. Once complete, the holders of the Bonesetter of Torfast Trading Post, Broker of Treji Wayhouse, Overseer of the Westward Road and Northbound Trademaster became able to trade materials for crystal mana. This trade remains viable only while the Empire stays at peace with the Thule.

n.Imperial Orcs: The road runs from the Torfast Trading Post in the Orc territory of Skarsind, giving the Orc-held trading post a direct route to the Thule for exchanging materials for crystal mana.
n.Thule: The road connects the Thule to the Empire's Torfast Trading Post, establishing a trade in materials for crystal mana that lasts only as long as the Empire and the Thule remain at peace.

t.Skarsind: The road was built from the Torfast Trading Post in Skarsind, proposed by Skarsind's senator, making the territory the Empire's trading gateway to the Thule.

Construct an inspirational shrine to Cor.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Bastion, the motion created a memorial shrine to Cora Holdfast, an exemplar of the Virtue of Loyalty, based in High Chalcis. The shrine was established as a self-funded religious sinecure, with its holder appointed by the Assembly of Loyalty. The motion passed in Summer 381YE. After the Summer Solstice, Cadeus provided the materials and costs for its construction: 10 wains of white granite, 10 wains of weirwood, 44 crowns and a dose of true liao.

n.Highguard: Highguard's senators for Reikos and Bastion proposed and seconded the motion, giving the nation a new shrine honouring an exemplar of Loyalty in one of its territories.

t.Reikos: High Chalcis in Reikos became home to the shrine to Cora Holdfast, with a new religious sinecure based there and appointed by the Assembly of Loyalty.

Construct the Glass Point Cove.d: Announced by Dalibor Marek do Saverio Von Temeschwar, a holder of an Imperial Wayleave exercising the power to commission constructions delegated by the Senate, the commission called for a mighty construction to harness the natural mana flows beneath the cliffs of Glass Point. It took the form of a mana sinecure with no upkeep. After the Summer Solstice, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided the 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns needed. Its completion automatically created the title of Custodian of Glass Point Cove, a national League position appointed by the Senators of the League.

n.The League: The League gained a new national title, the Custodian of Glass Point Cove, appointed by its Senators to control a mana sinecure that carries no upkeep.

t.Sarvos: Sarvos became home to the Glass Point Cove, a construction harnessing the mana flows beneath the cliffs of Glass Point.

r.Sarvos/Uccelini: The Glass Point Cove was built in Uccelini to draw on the natural mana flows beneath the region's Glass Point cliffs.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.d: Proposed by the senator for Temeschwar and seconded by Holberg, the motion called for a plantation of the most exquisite cultivars of Catazarro wines at the outskirts of the Aversa Estate in Foracci. The vineyards were to be under the jurisdiction of the Vine Tender of the Signori d'Argento Vineyards, a national League position appointed by the League Senators, as a self-funded money sinecure with no upkeep. Although the motion passed, it was abrogated by the Senate at the Summer Solstice 381YE. Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower, as holder of an Imperial Wayleave, later recommissioned it.

n.The League: The vineyards would create a new League national position, the Vine Tender, appointed by the League Senators and holding a self-funded money sinecure built on Catazarro wine cultivars.

t.Sarvos: The League territory of Sarvos was the chosen site for the vineyards. The project was abrogated after passing and was later recommissioned under an Imperial Wayleave.

r.Sarvos/Foracci: The vineyards were to be planted at the outskirts of the Aversa Estate in Foracci, bringing fine Catazarro wine cultivars to the region.

Construct the Signori d’Argento Vineyard.d: The announcement revived a previous plan to build a vineyard money sinecure in Sarvos, which had been the subject of an earlier Senate motion that was later abrogated. Rather than going back through the Senate, Brother Dagon of the Shattered Tower used the power to commission constructions that the Senate delegates to holders of an Imperial Wayleave. After the Summer Solstice 381YE, Giacomo Corvinoscuro provided 10 wains of weirwood and 20 crowns towards the work. The vineyards were to be completed by the Autumn Equinox 381YE, creating the title of Signori d'Argento Vine Tender.

n.The League: A new League sinecure, the Signori d'Argento Vine Tender, was set to be created through vineyards in Sarvos, funded with weirwood and crowns from Giacomo Corvinoscuro.

t.Sarvos: The Signori d'Argento Vineyards were to be built in Sarvos and completed by the Autumn Equinox 381YE.

Construct the market town of New Dunhall.d: Proposed by the senator for Sermersuaq and seconded by the Conscience, the motion passed at a cost of 30 Thrones. It created a new market town near the ruins of Dunhall in Hahnmark, to be overseen by a new title, the Caretaker of New Dunhall, which will generate coin. The motion framed the work as the beginning of recovery from the catastrophic loss of Dunhearth Hall in the recent collapse. After the Summer Solstice, Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason provided the 20 wains of white granite and 40 crowns needed. The town was due to be complete by the Autumn Equinox 381YE. The proposing senator indicated that the Caretaker will be a Wintermark national appointment.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new market town in its own territory, and the Caretaker of New Dunhall is to be appointed by the Wintermark nation, giving the Steinr, Suaq and Kallavesi a new sinecure that generates coin.

t.Hahnmark: New Dunhall is to rise near the ruins of Dunhall in Hahnmark, beginning the territory's recovery from the catastrophic loss of Dunhearth Hall in the recent collapse.

Construct trade hub in Upwold.d: Proposed by Upwold and seconded by Bregasland, the motion split the cost between the Marches and Lady Sarelta of the Red Moon of the Faraden. The minimum cost was estimated at 20 wains of weirwood, 20 wains of white granite and 80 crowns. The Faraden committed to supplying the white granite and 40 crowns towards labour, and offered to match the Empire's weirwood and half the labour costs if a larger enclave was built. After the Autumn Equinox 381YE, Henry Ward provided 20 wains of weirwood and 5 thrones. Once complete, the hub was expected to act as a great work giving Marcher citizens who own farms and businesses a share of funds. The Senate abrogated it in Spring 384YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches were to pay half the cost of the hub, and Marcher citizens who own farms and businesses stood to receive a share of its funds until the Senate abrogated it in Spring 384YE.

t.Upwold: King's Stoke in Upwold was chosen as the site of the Faraden trade hub, which Upwold's own senator proposed.

Create law of protection for humans in M.d: Proposed by Mitwold and seconded by Morrow, the motion afforded legal protection to the humans of the Mourn other than the Feni. The court noted a contradiction: some of these humans were fighting for the Jotun, and enemies of the Empire ordinarily have no legal protection. Imperial soldiers facing them in battle would usually be covered by self-defence, but that defence carries a reasonableness test that could place soldiers' conduct under magistrates' scrutiny, and less clear-cut situations might arise during the Mourn campaign. The phrase "Humans of the Mourn" covers people living in the Mourn even when they are outside it, but not barbarian humans whose homes lie elsewhere.

n.Jotun: Humans fighting for the Jotun in the Mourn are now legally protected, which complicates Imperial efforts against Jotun forces by exposing soldiers to possible scrutiny from magistrates.

t.Mournwold: The Jotun-held Mournwold's non-Feni human inhabitants gained legal protection equivalent to foreigners, wherever they happen to be, which shapes how the Empire can conduct its campaign there.

Death is not the end.d: Priests from seven nations had shrunk Yael's congregation in Reikos, and their returning pilgrims now spoke out against her. Armies from opposing sides of the schism lost a fifth of their victory points when campaigning together, and military units supporting the other side had their effective ranks halved. Highguard's acceptance of Yael brought a surge in prosperity. Highborn supporters urged a foundationalist mandate declaring their assembly the sole authority on doctrine, which risked a deep rift with the Empire. Condemnation for heresy by the General Assembly or the Council of Nine was set out as the way to bring Yael to trial. Dawn's assembly then passed a mandate repudiating Yael, carried by Odelina de Rondell.

n.Dawn: Having first sung Yael's praises and then rejected a mandate to spread her song, the Dawnish assembly ended the confusion at the Summer Solstice by repudiating her, with Odelina de Rondell taking liao to call Dawnish pilgrims home and placing Dawn among the nations that reject her.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Reikos is described as reclaimed from the Druj and reborn, one of the signs Highborn take as heralding a new era.
n.Highguard: Highguard's embrace of Yael brought a surge of national confidence and prosperity, while supporters pressed for a foundationalist mandate making the Highborn Assembly the sole authority on doctrine, risking open conflict with the rest of the Empire. Doubters urged the assembly to reconsider.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs declared themselves no part of this dispute over human destiny, so their armies suffered no penalty and could fight effectively alongside either side of the schism.
n.Navarr: As one of the seven nations that rejected Yael, Navarr had sent a priest to call its people home from Reikos, and its armies now fought less effectively when campaigning beside Highborn or Dawnish forces.
n.The Marches: The Marches, having rejected Yael and sent a priest to bring its pilgrims home, saw returning Marchers turn against her, and its armies were penalised when campaigning alongside the other side of the schism.
n.Urizen: Urizen was among the seven nations that denounced Yael and recalled their pilgrims, and its armies suffered reduced effectiveness when fighting together with Highborn or Dawnish armies.
n.Varushka: Varushka had sent a priest to repudiate Yael and return its people from Reikos, and its armies now faced a penalty when campaigning beside armies from nations that embraced her.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark, one of the nations that rejected Yael, had brought its pilgrims home, and its armies were penalised when fighting alongside forces from the other side of the schism.

t.Bastion: Bastion, long the spiritual heart of the Way, stood to have that role challenged by a foundationalist mandate, and the Illuminators of Shadow scriptorium there announced they would bring a precious gift for the First Empress.
t.Casinea: Devout pilgrims of the First Empress in Casinea could be recruited into the Granite Pillar if the foundationalist mandate were enacted, and at Mareholm Jerusha of the Black Watch preached against Yael's rejection of the Synod.
t.Reikos: Reikos, hailed as restored and reborn, was where Yael's congregation gathered; it shrank as the seven nations' priests drew pilgrims home, though its devoted pilgrims remained a possible source of recruits for the Granite Pillar.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold appears only in the name of Cathy Upwold, one of the seven sent to Reikos to persuade pilgrims to abandon Yael.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: Jerusha of the Black Watch at Mareholm delivered a pointed sermon arguing that no true reincarnation of the First Empress would reject the Synod's judgement, so Yael's defiance proved her false.

Distribute food to the thralls of Mournw.d: Proposed by the senator for Morrow and seconded by the senator for Redoubt, the motion arose from opportunities in the Mournwold and called for 75 thrones of food to be given to the thralls living there. The Senate passed it, and the 75 thrones needed were provided by Orrick of House Bolholt. The page gives no further detail of what followed once the food had been distributed.

n.Jotun: The Senate sent Imperial food to the thralls living under Jotun rule in the Mournwold, reaching people within the orcs' conquered lands.

t.Mournwold: The thralls of the Jotun-held Mournwold were to receive 75 thrones' worth of food, paid for by Orrick of House Bolholt.

Down along the cove.d: Fisherfolk from Feroz, Madruga, Necropolis, Sarvos, Redoubt and Tassato could profit by pushing into deeper waters, but Grendel captains sought slaves, boats and dredged-up ilium. The Fellowship of Purple Sails, Freeborn corsair families, Ferozi and Madrugan paradors and League guilds offered a 3-crown bounty to fleets protecting the fishermen. Too little protection would see businesses lose a fifth of production and a permanent drop in taxes; enough would bring extra production, and greater efforts more ilium at auction and a richer Broken Shore Bounty, though this might push Grendel towards foreign traders. Synod mandates could urge captains to defend the fleet or, alternatively, urge caution and cancel the opportunity entirely.

n.Grendel: Independent Grendel captains, not tied up in the Spiral campaign, were drawn to the Bay to seize crews as slaves, boats, cargo and ilium from Imperial fisherfolk; strong Imperial protection would drive them off, perhaps towards ships trading through the southern bay.
n.Highguard: Highborn fishermen off the Necropolis coast, like Captain Amos of Candle Cove, saw the moonfish boom first-hand, and Necropolis businesses stood to gain or lose depending on how well the fleet was protected.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsair families and the paradors of Feroz and Madruga helped fund the bounty for protecting fishermen, and Freeborn captains taking the action would count it towards the Broken Shore Bounty, which could rise if protection was strong.
n.The League: League guilds involved with fishing helped fund the protection bounty, while Sarvos and Tassato's businesses stood to profit or suffer depending on whether the Grendel raids were stopped.
n.Urizen: Redoubt, which draws some of its prosperity from the sea, was among the territories whose businesses would gain extra production or lose a fifth of it, along with some permanent tax revenue, depending on the outcome.

t.Bay of Catazar: The magic worked on the Bay produced a boom in fish and sea creatures, and its open waters became the hunting ground of both bold Imperial fisherfolk and Grendel raiders.
t.Feroz: Feroz's businesses risked losing a fifth of their production and suffering one of the most severe permanent tax drops if the Grendel raids succeeded, but would gain extra production if the fleet was protected; Ferozi paradors helped fund the bounty.
t.Madruga: Madrugan paradors helped back the bounty, as the territory's businesses faced either bumper profits or one of the heaviest losses in production and permanent tax revenue should the Grendel prevail.
t.Necropolis: Fishing boats off the Necropolis coast were hauling up unusually large moonfish, and the territory's businesses and tax revenue depended on whether Imperial fleets kept the Grendel away.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's partly sea-based businesses could gain extra production or lose a fifth of it, along with some permanent tax revenue, depending on how well the fishing fleet was protected.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's fishing concerns stood to profit from the boom, but a successful Grendel raid would cost its businesses a fifth of their production and cause one of the worst permanent drops in taxes.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies were noted as being engaged in the Spiral campaign, leaving independent captains free to prey on fishermen.
t.Tassato: Tassato's businesses would gain extra production if the fishermen were protected or lose a fifth of it if raided, though the loss of boats would not reduce its tax revenue.

In Virtue and Reason.d: Delivered by the civil service to citizens across the Empire and beyond, the address argued in Virtue that eradicating another culture could never be a true Legacy or Inspiration, and that Jotun children are not monsters to be scourged. In Reason, it held that slaughtering civilians escalates war into a struggle for survival, whereas wars are won when foes know they are beaten. Lisabetta praised the response to her coronation call, noting that the Valiant Pegasus had become an army of physicks, and commended Raewynn Farkas's proposed Conclave order, the Silver Chalice, devoted to magical healing. She also named the Generals of seven armies who had ordered their troops to spare civilians.

n.Jotun: The Throne acknowledged that the Mournwold campaign had dealt a terrible blow to Jotun armies but had also killed many Jotun non-combatants, and declared that the children of the Jotun are not monsters to be scourged, calling them future citizens and allies.
n.Navarr: The Navarr Raewynn Farkas was singled out for praise for her plan to found the Silver Chalice, a new Conclave order dedicated to using magic to heal body and mind in partnership with Imperial healers.

t.Mournwold: Fighting in the Jotun-held Mournwold the previous season killed far more civilians who till the soil and raise families than soldiers, prompting the Throne's call to stop targeting non-combatants there.

Not dark yet.d: The Freeborn, Marcher and Wintermark assemblies had condemned the Iron Helms' cruelty, while the Varushkan and Navarr assemblies backed it. The Iron Helms had arrested Dogri Thulebane at Crow's Keep and then waged a merciless onslaught against the Jotun in the Mourn. Gunnbrand Ironwill took 50 liao for Wintermark to shun the Iron Helms and show true heroism. Constanza i Kalamar i Guerra took 25 liao for the Freeborn to reject them. Amris Johan Merikovich took 100 liao for Varushka to show real cruelty, giving the Iron Helms the dark-magic order Terror in the Night. Corey Wayfarer took 75 liao for Navarr, so the Quiet Step may become a Cunning army. The Marcher option was not taken up.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is named as a nation attacked by the Druj, and its lands were among those where an unenacted Varushkan mandate would have strengthened Varushkan defenders.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj resurgence in the east is cited as the threat to Karsk, Dawn and Urizen that some Varushkans argued their armies should face instead of the Jotun.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, but the Iron Helms' action against the rebel Dogri Thulebane took place in Skarsind, which the Imperial Orcs held.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces in the Mourn suffered the Iron Helms' merciless onslaught, and the Varushkan mandate now lets the Iron Helms send night terrors into Jotun dreams to break their armies. The Marcher option to fight them with restraint was not enacted.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly had declared the Iron Helms' cruel tactics virtuous, then sent Corey Wayfarer with 75 liao. The general of the Quiet Step may now permanently make the army Cunning by supplying 50 wains of weirwood.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's Holberg was named among territories where Varushkan armies would have gained a defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Urizen is named as attacked by the Druj, and its lands were among those where an unenacted Varushkan mandate would have aided Varushkan defenders.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan assembly defended the Iron Helms and sent Amris Johan Merikovich with 100 liao. Until the Spring Equinox 382YE, dark spirits, cabals and wolves accompany the army, letting its general order Terror in the Night for 25 mana crystals.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark sent Gunnbrand Ironwill with 50 liao, so for a year its soldiers shun the Iron Helms, reducing that army's victory points when they campaign together. Wintermark generals fighting alongside the Iron Helms may also order a triumphant charge or final stand.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg was listed where Varushkan armies would have gained a 10% defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk is described as once again directly threatened by Druj barbarians, a reason given for turning Varushkan armies east.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven was listed among places where Varushkan orders would have been restricted under a mandate that was not enacted.
t.Mournwold: The Iron Helms' cruelty against the Jotun in the Mourn was seen by Winterfolk, Freeborn and Marchers, prompting these mandates. The Quiet Step's tactics there also stirred debate among the Navarr.
t.Skarsind: In Skarsind the Iron Helms crushed Dogri Thulebane's rebellion, destroyed Crow's Keep and carried him in chains to Anvil, angering many Winterfolk.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin was listed where Varushkan armies would have gained a defensive bonus under a mandate that was not enacted.

Pay in blood.d: The loss affected every regio, including those in conquered territories, but only Imperial citizens; foreign magicians could still use them. The regio and their portals remain, but no Imperial citizen can use a regio to strengthen a Spring ritual, target one at a territory through the Imperial regio, or affect a whole territory from a local regio. Rituals such as Rivers of Life, Thunderous Deluge and Hallow of the Green World have become impossible to perform. Workarounds such as the Citadel Guard's targeting or Align the Celestial Net also fail. No divination could detect the cause. How long it will last, and whether anything can be done, is unknown; the earlier loss lasted four seasons.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, but Liathaven, which they hold, is cited as a conquered territory whose regio are closed to Imperial magicians.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the ritual The Dance of Navarr and Thorn is listed among the Spring rituals that can no longer be performed.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a Thule coven is given as an example of foreign magicians who can still use a Spring regio inside the Empire's borders.
n.Urizen: Urizen magicians were quick to identify that their Spring regios had lost their power entirely, and like all Imperial citizens they can no longer use them for Spring rituals.

t.Liathaven: Liathaven is named as a conquered territory whose regio are also closed to Imperial magicians for Spring magic, though others can still use them.

Recognise ducal quality.d: The motion, proposed by the senator for Astolat and seconded by the senator for Mitwold, declared that the Empire wished to recognise the Ducal Quality of Kalino, a land of the Iron Confederacy, and to open a continuing dialogue for mutual benefit. It passed. As a statement of the Senate it carried no legal force within the Empire, but it was noted that it might have diplomatic consequences for relations with the Iron Confederacy.

t.Kalino: The Senate formally acknowledged Kalino's ducal standing within the Iron Confederacy, a diplomatic gesture that could shape future dealings between the Empire and its rulers.

Research Aneira Dancewalker and her brot.d: Announced in Summer 381YE, the research request was made under the power to announce historical research that the Senate has delegated to the Dredgemaster of Feverwater. It concerns two figures from Liathaven's past. Aneira Dancewalker is thought to have been General of the Quiet Step at the time Liathaven fell. Her brother Eurion Dancewalker forged Aneira's Talon, an improved version of the Scorpion's Sting. The pair are believed to have lived in a steading in West Ranging. At the time of the record the research was still in progress, and no findings had been reported.

n.Jotun: The Jotun held Liathaven that season, and the research looked into figures from the history of the land they now controlled.

t.Liathaven: The research focuses on Liathaven's past: a general of the Quiet Step at the time of its fall, and the smith who forged Aneira's Talon there.

r.Liathaven/West Ranging: West Ranging is believed to have been home to the Dancewalker siblings' steading, making it the likely focus of the research.

Rocks and gravel.d: About a month after the Spring Equinox, north-western Goldglades collapsed. Vates' warnings from the Pool of Silver Clouds limited the loss of life. The hole spread for a month, swallowing Woodhall in Hahnmark and part of the Vardstein Vales, and forcing Eastern Guard's evacuation before it stopped. The result is a seven-hundred-foot sinkhole with a possibly bottomless lake and tunnels reaching back to Terunael times and earlier. Miaren and Hahnmark are no longer adjacent, and armies can no longer move between Temeschwar and Upwold. Military units may loot the weltsilver, but too many would rouse the trogoni to attack nearby territories. The Senate or Military Council could intervene. The opportunity lasts six months.

n.Navarr: The collapse began in Navarr's Miaren, where vates foresaw it in the Pool of Silver Clouds and sent warnings to the threatened regions. Navarr armies can no longer move directly between Miaren and Hahnmark.
n.The League: The League's Temeschwar lost part of the Vardstein Vales to the sinkhole, and campaign armies can no longer move between Temeschwar and Upwold.
n.The Marches: Sinkholes opened in north-eastern Upwold and the old fortress of Eastern Guard was evacuated. Upwold is now cut off from Temeschwar for army movement and lies in the path of any trogoni outbreak.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: trogoni are described as rarely encountered outside the mountains of Urizen, and the opening story features a Urizen mage.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: trogoni are said to be otherwise found mainly in the northern peaks of Wintermark and Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Hahnmark lost Woodhall, which was swallowed whole, and the lands around Dunhearth Hall were badly hit. Hahnmark is no longer adjacent to Miaren and faces danger if the trogoni are roused.

t.Hahnmark: Woodhall in the far south-west was swallowed a day after Navarr warnings arrived, with the thane's quick action saving hundreds. The lands around Dunhearth Hall were badly damaged, and Hahnmark is no longer adjacent to Miaren.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the opening story refers to a smuggling ring in the Holberg swamps where an adventurer was eaten by a marshwalker.
t.Miaren: A half-mile section of north-western Goldglades collapsed, starting the sinkhole. Miaren is no longer adjacent to Hahnmark and is one of four territories threatened by any trogoni outbreak.
t.Temeschwar: Sinkholes opened in south-eastern Temeschwar and a significant part of the Vardstein Vales slid into the hole. Armies can no longer move between Temeschwar and Upwold.
t.Upwold: Sinkholes opened in north-eastern Upwold and Eastern Guard was evacuated for weeks. Campaign armies can no longer travel between Upwold and Temeschwar.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath was warned of the spreading collapse and borders the new sinkhole, near where Woodhall was swallowed in Hahnmark's far south-west.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: One of Miaren's richest regions, Goldglades saw a half-mile section of its north-west collapse first. Vates' warnings let many Navarr escape.
r.Upwold/Birchland: Birchland received Navarr warnings as the hole spread and is one of the four regions bordering the sinkhole and its trogoni-infested tunnels.

Series of dreams.d: Stars stayed hidden across most of the Empire, strengthening naga secretiveness. Skies were clear over Morrow, Spiral, Redoubt and Skarsind, while a Penumbral Veil settled on Zenith. The Archmage of Summer apparently persuaded Cathan Canae to lift the storm over the Icy Crag, and a contest will decide its patron. Koboldi sent by Barien built the Empress of All Goats Theatre in Veresk for Hubert Annanovich Gremani. Magical citadels raised in Kahraman and Bregasland faded unused when no Jotun attack came. Urizeni realigned the Ribbon of Salt to Night just before it exploded, inflaming the Freeborn Storm navy's passions. Heralds of Murit and Soghter rendered orc corpses for the Azoth. Two rituals entered Imperial Lore.

n.Druj: The Barrens remained beneath the starless sky, and the Urizen blamed Druj invaders for conjuring the Penumbral Veil that settled over Zenith.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Spiral, held by the Grendel, is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.
n.Highguard: Casinea, home of Anvil, stayed under the starless sky, and in Reikos Llofir kept its living fungal castle in Tamarbode, which Highborn magisters judged to be playing a long game.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories with clear night skies, so naga living there were free of the shroud's influence.
n.Jotun: Their Mournwold and Liathaven stayed starless, the Imperial citadels raised against them in Kahraman and Bregasland faded when no Jotun attack came, and Night heralds harvested dead orcs from the Mournwold battlefields.
n.Navarr: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a Frozen Citadel above Serra Damata, Navarr vates watched Llofir's Tamarbode warily, and a Navarr wayhouse sheltered Hubert while his home was demolished.
n.The Brass Coast: A keep of black ice guarded Serra Damata, and the Freeborn Storm navy, sailing off Redoubt, felt the Ribbon of Embers inflame their passions, fuelling sudden friendships and bitter feuds.
n.The Marches: The Sussivari Frost Coven's fog-wrapped citadels protected Bregasland unopposed, and in the shared Mournwold Night heralds harvested dead orcs and the occasional Feni.
n.Urizen: Morrow and Redoubt had clear skies but Zenith fell under a Penumbral Veil, and heroic Urizeni realigned the Ribbon of Salt to Night just before it exploded, leaving locals with strange dreams.
n.Varushka: Koboldi sent by Barien demolished playwright Hubert Annanovich Gremani's home in Veresk and built the Temeschwari-style Empress of All Goats Theatre in its place, his reward for completing a challenge.

t.Bregasland: Dripping Echoes of the Fen settled as fog and whispers over Grey Fens and Ottermire, then faded when no Jotun invasion arrived.
t.Casinea: Casinea stayed under the starless sky, so naga attending the summit at Anvil felt their urge towards secrecy strengthen, though the skies directly over Anvil appeared normal.
t.Kahraman: A Frozen Citadel of black ice was raised above Serra Damata against a possible Jotun attack and faded once none came.
t.Karsk: In the vale of Veresk, twenty koboldi built the Empress of All Goats Theatre over Hubert Annanovich Gremani's former home, a tiny folly that drew growing interest.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven is named among the neighbouring territories whose night skies stayed empty of stars.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow is listed among the territories with clear night skies, freeing its naga from the shroud's influence.
t.Mournwold: The skies stayed starless, and Night heralds of Murit and Soghter came out of Alderly and Freemoor to boil unburied orc corpses in black cauldrons, leaving barren circles behind.
t.Redoubt: Redoubt's skies were clear, but the Ribbon of Salt off Visten erupted as a torrent of Night magic and subsided into vents of ash and embers, leaving odd dreams and phenomena.
t.Reikos: Tamarbode remained claimed by Llofir, its ever-changing fungal castle looming over a forest closed to Imperial citizens except the mana site at Tamar's Toes.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Skarsind is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Spiral is listed among the territories where the night skies were clear.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens are named among the neighbouring territories still beneath the starless sky.
t.Zenith: The empty sky lifted from Zenith, but a Penumbral Veil settled over the territory, which the Urizen blamed on Druj invaders.

r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: A Dripping Echo of the Fen covered Grey Fens in fog and whispers to resist a possible Jotun invasion, fading when none came.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: A Dripping Echo of the Fen shrouded Ottermire against a possible Jotun attack before dissipating unused.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Eternal Family of Navarr raised a keep of black ice above Serra Damata, which faded when no Jotun attack materialised.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Scaled and feathered Night heralds emerged from Alderly's shadowy woodlands to harvest unburied orc corpses in bubbling cauldrons.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Night heralds came out of Freemoor's chalk barrows to render dead orcs for the Azoth, leaving circles where no grass will grow.
r.Redoubt/Optarion: The Ribbon of Salt off Visten, realigned to Night by Urizeni heroes, exploded in shadows and embers, then subsided to occasional vents, with locals reporting peculiar dreams.
r.Reikos/Tamarbode: Llofir still held Tamarbode, whose living fungal castle enclosed the Sign of Tamar regio, and mana gatherers at Tamar's Toes told of watching creatures and strange moulds.

Shelter from the storm.d: The Isle of Zemress, settled by the crew of the mariner Zemress a century and a half ago, had been recognised by the Freeborn assembly in 380YE, and Freeborn missionaries had persuaded its Prosperity-focused people to value all seven Virtues. Grendel privateers then found the island and gathered to loot it and carry the islanders off as slaves. Dhomiro Tevus i Zemress appealed to Sol i Riqueza for aid. Independent Imperial captains could attempt an evacuation during the Summer downtime only. Success would depend on the fleet strength committed, ranging from total enslavement to a full rescue with all possessions. Grateful islanders offered payment to participating captains. The Synod could mandate captains to help, and the Quartermaster General could extend the Guerdon to the effort.

n.Grendel: Grendel pirate and slaving vessels, rather than a full navy, gathered to descend on the island to loot it and take its people to places such as the salt mines of Dubhtraig. Their privateers would be beaten back, blockaded or routed depending on how strongly Imperial captains responded.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn faced the loss of cousins they had recently recognised as entitled to Brass Coast citizenship and had converted to the full Way. The Freeborn assembly could pass a mandate pressing Freeborn captains to join the rescue, and a successful one would bring refugees and new wealth to their lands.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Isle of Zemress lies within the Bay of Catazar, well outside Imperial waters, where Grendel privateers were massing to attack it. Any rescue would require Imperial ships to run or break their blockade through treacherous waters.
t.Feroz: Feroz was one of two destinations for rescued islanders if the evacuation achieved sufficient strength. A complete rescue would see new resources established there by the exiles, eventually raising its tax revenue.
t.Madruga: Madruga was the other destination for evacuated Zemress islanders, who might arrive destitute or with enough wealth to prosper, depending on the rescue's success. A complete rescue would add new resources run by the exiles, increasing its tax revenue over time.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel navies engaged in Spiral were cited as an obstacle that the Freeborn Storm would need to get past to reach the island.

Too much of nothing.d: With the Tower of Dawn fallen and the Barrens lost, Earl Hugo the Scarred of House Renard led his many destitute yeofolk towards Semmerholm. He came to Anvil to sell a single box of Barrenberry seeds, the only stock outside Druj-held Drycastle, to feed them through winter. Sir Morold Lionsgate's seneschal sought a buyer for incomplete writings by a long-dead Dawnish senator, to fund a memorial to Morold's grandmother. A young Steinr, cast out after the mysterious drowning of the Suaq icewalker Ilma Erkking, offered an ancient skinning knife from a cave. Felipa i Manola i Guerra brought an uninvestigated curio said to come from a freeborn exemplar of Prosperity's tomb.

n.Dawn: Dawn's loss of Drycastle left House Renard's yeofolk homeless and hungry, forcing Earl Hugo to sell the last Barrenberry seeds. Sir Morold Lionsgate's seneschal also offered a dead Dawnish senator's writings, looking for buyers first in the Dawnish camp.
n.Druj: The Druj had taken Drycastle and expelled the Imperial presence from the Barrens. This left the renowned Renard vineyards and their Barrenberry grapes in orcish hands.

t.Semmerholm: Ancient families and House Renard's many farm workers, driven out of the Barrens, made their way to the relative safety of Semmerholm's wooded glades. They arrived with no harvest to see them through the coming winter.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: the seneschal wondered whether someone from Weirwater might be interested in a past senator's writings.

Under the red sky.d: Syrus Skybreaker's second missive to Tharim brought the herald Shakle, who confirmed a formal parley with The Three at midnight on the Friday. Tharim wished to discuss forging chains to take on part of his curse. Skathe wished to discuss fashion, and Surut asked for a formal representative of Imperatrix Lisabetta. Llofir declined parley but promised messenger heralds. Roshanwe announced that 'The Mariner' would come to discuss the Symposium. Lashonar accepted a challenge of music and song for the Winter Solstice and returned an unopened note to Murit. Barien said the Summer nobles had accepted a tournament for patronage of the Icy Crag, to be held no earlier than Autumn, and that the icy winds over Volchitrava had stopped.

n.Varushka: The icy winds that had been damaging the Varushkan vale of Volchitrava stopped, with no current sign of Cathan Canae's anger, though Cathan Canae is among the Summer eternals sending heralds to find champions.

t.Miekarova: The damaging icy winds over the vale of Volchitrava ceased this season, and Cathan Canae's anger showed no sign of returning for the moment.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The vale of Volchitrava gained relief as the icy winds tied to Cathan Canae's anger stopped blowing.

When the ship comes in.d: Missionaries working with Bonewall Rek were well received in the Commonwealth, Asavea and Sarcophan, but less so in Jarm, where the Sumaah urged caution. No schism was expected. Asavean families arrived to use the new Cavabianca Dock but docked in Oran, insisting it should have been built there rather than in Sarvos. Axos kept paying high prices for liao. Rigia grew less welcoming. A Sumaah delegation landed at Crown's Quay to pursue an inquisition of Bonewall Rek and Cole. Faraden laid the i Tsagaan matter uneasily to rest. The Delves had a surplus of Cerulean Mazzarine. The Commonwealth remained frosty, and the Thule refused to recognise the new Ambassador.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders are said to be slowly becoming more common in western Dawn as stretches of the Blood Red Roads near completion.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Empire is technically at peace with the Druj, but it is unclear how long that will last given recent developments in Dawnguard, and there is no trade with them.
n.Grendel: The Commonwealth showed little interest in joining the Empire's campaign against the Grendel. Rumours spread of a Sarcophan agreement with the Grendel to keep access to Imperial ports, and of Sarcophan merchants reselling Imperial goods at a profit in Dubhtraig.
n.Highguard: Chesed of High House preached the new Doctrines to a Commonwealth congregation in Leerdam. The Faraden investigator concluded that Ephrael of Highguard's killing of Laodicia i Tsagaan was almost certainly provoked. A Sumaah delegation landed at Crown's Quay in Necropolis.
n.Navarr: The Great Forest orcs and their human allies remain in Navarri-held Therunin, though they and the Empire are now actively discussing a treaty.
n.The Brass Coast: An Asavean ship docked at Oran in Feroz, claiming the white granite docks were meant to be built there. The Freeborn welcome to Asavean visitors had already boosted local paradour owners, and Faraden traders are common on the Brass Coast.
n.The League: The newly completed Cavabianca Dock in Sarvos risks going unused because the Asavean families expected it in Oran. Meanwhile, the Lodge in Tassato has helped keep relations with Jarm cordial.
n.Thule: The Thule refused to recognise Ambassador Juha the Cavespider until the Empire builds an embassy in northern Varushka or lets the Varushkans appoint the title. They have not withdrawn their trade network offer or their interest in the Gildenheim Runeforge.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly's call for Commonwealth soldiers to join the campaign against the Grendel met little interest, as Commonwealth critics accused the Empire of hypocrisy over slavery.
n.Varushka: The Thule will deal with the Varushkan warlock Juha but demand an embassy in northern Varushka or a Varushkan-appointed ambassador. Faraden traders are also appearing more often in southern Varushka.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Asavean families' ship arrived on the Bay, and Sarcophan merchants are a common sight along its shores.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Faraden traders are a relatively common sight in Casinea.
t.Feroz: Members of the Heraclien and Ragnabe families docked at Oran rather than Sarvos, insisting their agreement placed the docks within sight of the temple there. A representative was expected at Anvil to speak to the Ambassador.
t.Necropolis: A Sumaah ship arrived at Crown's Quay, landing Tipoa the Insightful and an entourage bound for Anvil to pursue an inquisition into Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not named; the page only notes the Urizen Assembly's efforts to recruit Commonwealth soldiers for the campaign against the Grendel.
t.Sarvos: The Cavabianca Dock, built in the Sarvosan district of Caricomare for the Asavean white granite trade, may go unused unless the dispute over its intended location in Oran is resolved.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: the Lodge in Tassato is cited as aiding relations with Jarm, and Faraden traders are common there.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: there is no trade with the Barrens orcs, and peace with the Druj looks uncertain after events in Dawnguard.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest orcs and their human allies remain in Therunin with no sign of leaving, though treaty discussions with the Empire are now under way.

r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Mentioned in passing: recent developments in Dawnguard are cited as casting doubt on how long the Senate will stay at peace with the Druj.
